question: The total amount of electric charge that flows through a circuit is 1200 C in 2 min. Then the amount of electric current that is drawn by the same electric circuit is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The total electric charge (Q) that flows through the circuit is given as 1200 Coulombs (C).
 
• The time (t) taken for this charge to flow is 2 minutes, which is equivalent to 120 seconds (2 min x 60 sec/min).
 
• Electric current (I) is calculated using the formula I = Q / t.
 
• Substituting the given values, I = 1200 C / 120 s = 10 A.
 
• Thus, the electric current drawn by the circuit is 10 Amperes (A).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Current:**

 
 
• Electric current is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in Amperes (A), where 1 Ampere is equal to 1 Coulomb of charge passing through a point in 1 second.
 
 
 
• **Coulomb (C):**
 
 
• A Coulomb is the unit of electric charge in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• It is defined as the amount of charge transported by a constant current of one Ampere in one second.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Electric Current:**
 
 
• The formula to calculate electric current is I = Q / t, where I is the current, Q is the charge, and t is the time.
 
• This relationship helps in determining the current when the charge and time are known.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
